claims.title: Sofala recorded as a gold port
claims.summary: The geographer al-Masʿudi describes Muslim trade in the Sofala region; Sofala becomes the chief outlet for gold carried down from the interior highlands.

sources.label: A history of the medieval coastal towns of Mozambique (c. 500–1890 CE)

claims.title: Coastal trading towns flourish
claims.summary: Settlements at Sofala, Angoche, the Island of Mozambique, the Querimba Islands and the Zambezi mouth grow into nodes of the Swahili Indian Ocean trade.

sources.label: A history of the medieval coastal towns of Mozambique (c. 500–1890 CE)

claims.title: Kilwa controls the Sofala gold trade
claims.summary: The sultanate of Kilwa dominates the export of interior gold through Sofala, drawing wealth from the Zimbabwe and Mutapa goldfields into the wider Islamic world.

claims.title: Rise of the Mutapa state
claims.summary: The Mutapa (Monomotapa) state emerges on the Zimbabwean plateau, its gold and ivory passing down the Zambezi and out through the Mozambican ports.

sources.label: A history of the medieval coastal towns of Mozambique (c. 500–1890 CE)

claims.title: Vasco da Gama reaches the coast
claims.summary: Bound for India, Vasco da Gama anchors off the Island of Mozambique, where Muslim merchants receive him with suspicion; he sails on, marking the first European contact with the coast.

sources.label: Vasco da Gama
sources.publisher: The Mariners' Museum — Ages of Exploration

claims.title: Portuguese occupy Sofala
claims.summary: The Portuguese seize Sofala and build a fort to capture the gold trade, but find the port in decline and shift their base to the Island of Mozambique.

claims.title: Chapel of Nossa Senhora do Baluarte built
claims.summary: On the Island of Mozambique the Portuguese raise the small chapel of Nossa Senhora do Baluarte, often called the oldest surviving European building in the southern hemisphere.

Island of Mozambique UNESCO World Heritage Site

claims.title: Fort São Sebastião is built
claims.summary: Construction begins on Fort São Sebastião on the Island of Mozambique, the largest Portuguese fortress in East Africa and the oldest complete fort still standing in sub-Saharan Africa.

sources.label: Island of Mozambique — World Heritage List
Island of Mozambique UNESCO World Heritage Site

claims.title: Omanis take Fort Jesus at Mombasa
claims.summary: Omani Arabs capture Fort Jesus in Mombasa, rolling back Portuguese power on the northern Swahili coast and confining it largely to the territory of modern Mozambique.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1698-omanis-take-fort-jesus-at-mombasa, claim TL:MOZ:event:1698:omanis-take-fort-jesus-at-mombasa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Prazo estates along the Zambezi
claims.summary: The crown leases great estates, the prazos da coroa, to settlers along the Zambezi; their holders rule as semi-feudal lords with armies of slave-soldiers and a heavy stake in the slave trade.

sources.label: The History of Zambezia and Its Role in Mozambique's Colonial Economy

claims.title: Soshangane founds the Gaza Empire
claims.summary: Nguni warriors fleeing the upheavals of the Mfecane, led by Soshangane, conquer much of southern Mozambique and establish the Gaza Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1824-soshangane-founds-the-gaza-empire, claim TL:MOZ:event:1824:soshangane-founds-the-gaza-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Berlin Conference and the scramble
claims.summary: The Berlin Conference requires Portugal to occupy the territory it claims, spurring a drive to subdue the Mozambican interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1884-berlin-conference-and-the-scramble, claim TL:MOZ:event:1884:berlin-conference-and-the-scramble, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Defeat and capture of Gungunhana
claims.summary: Portuguese forces crush the Gaza army at Coolela and capture King Gungunhana at Chaimite, ending the Gaza Empire; he is exiled to the Azores, where he dies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1895-defeat-and-capture-of-gungunhana, claim TL:MOZ:event:1895:defeat-and-capture-of-gungunhana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mozambique Company chartered
claims.summary: The Mozambique Company receives a vast concession with powers to tax, govern and recruit labour, one of several chartered companies to which Portugal subcontracts colonial rule.

sources.label: The History of Zambezia and Its Role in Mozambique's Colonial Economy

claims.title: Estado Novo and tightened control
claims.summary: The authoritarian Estado Novo regime takes shape in Portugal, hardening colonial policy and entrenching forced labour and compulsory cultivation in Mozambique.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1926-estado-novo-and-tightened-control, claim TL:MOZ:event:1926:estado-novo-and-tightened-control, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Forced cotton cultivation and chibalo
claims.summary: Compulsory cotton-growing for Portuguese industry and the chibalo forced-labour system compel Mozambicans to grow cash crops and build infrastructure, causing hardship and hunger.

sources.label: Mozambique — forced labour and the slave trade

claims.title: Colonies redesignated 'overseas provinces'
claims.summary: Portugal renames its African colonies overseas provinces to resist decolonisation, while withholding citizenship and political rights from the African majority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1951-colonies-redesignated-overseas-provinces, claim TL:MOZ:event:1951:colonies-redesignated-overseas-provinces, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: FRELIMO is founded
claims.summary: Exiled nationalist groups unite in Dar es Salaam to form FRELIMO under Eduardo Mondlane, dedicated to ending Portuguese rule in Mozambique.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1962-frelimo-is-founded, claim TL:MOZ:event:1962:frelimo-is-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War of independence begins
claims.summary: FRELIMO launches its first armed attacks in Cabo Delgado, opening a decade-long guerrilla war against Portuguese colonial forces.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1964-war-of-independence-begins, claim TL:MOZ:event:1964:war-of-independence-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Eduardo Mondlane
claims.summary: FRELIMO's founding president is killed by a parcel bomb in Dar es Salaam; after a leadership struggle, Samora Machel emerges at the head of the movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1969-assassination-of-eduardo-mondlane, claim TL:MOZ:event:1969:assassination-of-eduardo-mondlane, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carnation Revolution and the Lusaka Accord
claims.summary: Lisbon's Carnation Revolution of April 1974 ends the dictatorship; in September Portugal and FRELIMO sign the Lusaka Accord, agreeing a transition to independence.

sources.label: Historical context: War and peace in Mozambique

claims.title: Independence of Mozambique
claims.summary: The People's Republic of Mozambique is proclaimed with Samora Machel as first president; most of the colony's Portuguese settlers depart, taking skills and capital with them.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1975-independence-of-mozambique, claim TL:MOZ:event:1975:independence-of-mozambique, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war and the rise of RENAMO
claims.summary: RENAMO, backed first by Rhodesia and then by apartheid South Africa, wages war on the FRELIMO government; the conflict devastates the countryside for fifteen years.

sources.label: Historical context: War and peace in Mozambique

claims.title: Death of Samora Machel
claims.summary: President Machel dies when his aircraft crashes near the South African border; Joaquim Chissano succeeds him and begins to move FRELIMO toward reform and negotiation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mozambique: From the gold ports of the Swahili coast to Portuguese conquest, a hard-won independence and a long road out of war.", terralore.co/country/MOZ/chronicle#ev-1986-death-of-samora-machel, claim TL:MOZ:event:1986:death-of-samora-machel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome General Peace Accords
claims.summary: Mediated by the Community of Sant'Egidio, President Chissano and RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama sign a peace agreement in Rome, ending a war that killed about a million people.

claims.title: First multiparty elections
claims.summary: Under UN supervision Mozambique holds its first multiparty elections, won by FRELIMO; the following year the country joins the Commonwealth.

claims.summary: Major natural-gas finds in the deep waters of the Rovuma basin attract tens of billions of dollars in planned investment and reshape the country's economic prospects.

claims.title: Cabo Delgado insurgency
claims.summary: An Islamist insurgency erupts in Cabo Delgado; its 2021 assault on Palma halts the main gas project, and the violence kills thousands and displaces close to a million people.
